items.prompt: A learner enrolled in version-1 of a course submits an attempt for a quiz that belongs to a newer draft version-2 of the same course. Why does checking only courseId not suffice, and what does the route do?
items.answer: Both versions share the courseId, so the route checks the quiz's courseVersionId and answers 404
distractors: courseId is enough, as drafts are unreachable by quiz id, and the attempt is recorded normally
The route accepts the attempt and tags it with the draft version so that it can be migrated later on
The route answers 403, as only instructors may submit attempts against a draft version
items.explanation: Every learner write must prove the content belongs to the ENROLLED version; `quiz.courseVersionId !== enrollment.courseVersionId` throws 404 "Quiz not found" before the transaction opens.

items.prompt: A published course's currentVersionId accidentally points at a DRAFT version. A new learner tries to enroll. What happens?
items.answer: The version lookup requires PUBLISHED, finds nothing, and enrollment fails with 404
distractors: The learner is enrolled in the draft, as the course row itself is PUBLISHED
The learner is silently enrolled in the newest PUBLISHED version of the course instead
Enrollment succeeds, but the learner sees no lessons until someone publishes the draft
items.explanation: Published selection has two parts: the course query requires PUBLISHED and the version query requires the pointer id, the same course and PUBLISHED - a stale or draft pointer yields "Published course version not found".

items.prompt: Two stored rules both set requireAssignmentsGraded: true. Rule A has requiredAssignmentIds: [] and rule B omits the field. How do they differ at completion?
items.answer: A requires no assignment; B derives every assignment of the enrolled version and requires each GRADED
distractors: Both require every assignment of the enrolled version; the parser coalesces [] to undefined
Both require nothing; requireAssignmentsGraded on its own never derives assignment ids
A requires every assignment and B requires none; only an explicit field turns the check on
items.explanation: completionRuleFor keeps an explicit array as-is and derives ids only when the field is omitted and the broad flag is on. The guide warns that coalescing [] to undefined would silently make a no-assessment course assessment-bound.

items.prompt: The rule lists requiredQuizIds: ["quiz-1"] with minimumQuizScore 80, and the learner has never attempted quiz-1. Why can completion not succeed?
items.answer: Each required id needs some matching passed attempt, and some() over no attempts is false
distractors: It can succeed: with no attempt the score defaults to 100, which meets the 80 minimum
It fails only when minimumQuizScore is set; without a minimum an absent attempt would pass
It fails as the route throws a 404 for any quiz that has no attempts recorded yet
items.explanation: Every required quiz id needs an attempt that is passed AND scores at least the minimum; `[].some(...)` is false, so there is no fallback that treats a missing attempt as passing.

items.prompt: A rule lists only one of the version's two lessons as required; the learner completes that one lesson (50% of progress rows). What does the completion request produce?
items.answer: The enrollment completes with its audit row and event, but no certificate is issued
distractors: A 409, as completion always requires every materialized lesson progress row to be COMPLETED
Completion plus a certificate, as the configured rule is fully satisfied by the one lesson
A certificate is created, but the enrollment stays IN_PROGRESS until the other lesson completes
items.explanation: Completion and certificate eligibility are separate: the rule permits completion, while canIssueCertificate demands completionPercent === 100, so the transaction writes everything except the certificate (certificateId undefined in payloads).

items.prompt: A lesson is marked COMPLETED, then IN_PROGRESS, then COMPLETED again. What happens to its timestamps?
items.answer: startedAt is kept; completedAt is cleared, then set to the new time, losing the first completion
distractors: completedAt keeps the first completion time; the ?? fallback preserves the earlier value
startedAt is reset by the IN_PROGRESS write, while completedAt is preserved across both of the writes
The second COMPLETED write is rejected; a lesson can only be completed once per enrollment
items.explanation: `completedAt: status === COMPLETED ? (current.completedAt ?? now) : null` - the IN_PROGRESS write nulls it, so the ?? fallback has nothing to preserve on the next completion.

items.prompt: A randomized quiz attempt request fails and its transaction rolls back. The learner retries. Which questions do they get, and why does that matter?
items.answer: The same set: the seed uses attemptCount, which the rolled-back request never incremented
distractors: A fresh random set: the selection seed includes the request timestamp
A fresh set: the failed attempt had already incremented the attemptCount before the rollback
The previous attempt's questions: they are reused so scores stay comparable
items.explanation: selectRandomizedQuestionIds is seeded with `${enrollmentId}-${attemptCount + 1}`; a rolled-back request leaves attemptCount unchanged, so the retry is deterministic.

items.prompt: Two first-time completion requests for the same enrollment arrive simultaneously and no certificate is issued for this rule. What happens, and what is the smallest fix?
items.answer: Both pass the guard and commit duplicate audit rows and events; predicate the update on status
distractors: The second request blocks on the pre-read; it returns the replay result, so nothing is duplicated
Certificate.enrollmentId @unique rejects the second request; that P2002 is mapped to a 409
Prisma serializes interactive transactions per row, so the second sees COMPLETED and returns early
items.explanation: The terminal guard is a read before the transaction and the update has no status predicate. Without a certificate there is no unique constraint to collide on, so both commit two audit rows, two events and outbox messages.

items.prompt: Two concurrent attempts both read attemptCount = n under READ COMMITTED when maxAttempts is n + 1. Is the retake limit exceeded?
items.answer: No: the unique attemptNumber constraint stops it, but the loser gets an unmapped 500
distractors: Yes: both attempts are created, as the count runs inside each transaction separately
No: READ COMMITTED makes the second read wait and see n + 1, so it answers a clean 409
Yes: but only when randomizeQuestionOrder is enabled, as that path skips the count
items.explanation: The schema's @@unique on attemptNumber holds the limit; the fix the review asks for is mapping that P2002 to 409 "Quiz retake limit reached" (or retrying once).

items.prompt: What is wrong with verificationCode = CERT- plus the last 8 characters of the enrollment id?
items.answer: Anyone who sees the enrollment id can compute it, and two ids with the same tail collide
distractors: Nothing serious: the verify route requires authentication, so a guessed code reveals nothing
Only that it is hard to read aloud; collisions are impossible as ids are random cuids
It changes whenever the enrollment is re-completed, which invalidates earlier shared links
items.explanation: The public verify route returns learner name and course title; the code must be an independent random value retried on collision, not a function of an id that appears in URLs.

items.prompt: A real outbox relay crashes between publishing a message and marking it sent. Why is this the failure order the guide prefers over marking sent first?
items.answer: A crash then causes a duplicate, which consumers can de-duplicate; marking first loses the message
distractors: Marking after publishing guarantees exactly-once delivery; a duplicate can never reach a consumer
Marking first is preferred; a lost message is cheaper to repair than a duplicated one
The order stops mattering once the relay claims rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a lease
items.explanation: Delivery becomes at-least-once; the guide contrasts that with today's worker, which marks 25 PENDING rows SENT without publishing anything and without a lease.

items.prompt: Why did the enrollment route stop mapping any error with code === "P2002" to 409?
items.answer: Any object with code P2002 - even from an unrelated helper - would be reported as already enrolled
distractors: Prisma renamed its unique-violation code in a recent release, so the old check never matched
The 409 leaked whether other users were enrolled, so the mapping had to become stricter
An instanceof check is cheaper than reading a property on every single error that reaches the catch
items.explanation: When mapping an error to a status code, match the error's type and its code, not the shape of a property - the test constructs a real PrismaClientKnownRequestError and a look-alike that must NOT map.

items.front: The assignment upsert's update branch sets content, status SUBMITTED and submittedAt unconditionally (learner.routes.ts:231-235). What goes wrong and what is the fix?
items.back: Resubmitting a GRADED submission flips it back to SUBMITTED while keeping score, feedback and grader - a contradictory row - and it works even on COMPLETED/DROPPED enrollments. Refuse resubmission of GRADED work and require enrollment.status ACTIVE before any learner write.

items.front: GET /catalog/courses/:courseId looks the course up by id alone and includes posts with author: true and quiz options (catalog.routes.ts:82-86). What leaks?
items.back: Cross-tenant data: draft versions, quiz options with isCorrect (answer keys), and full User scalars including email and passwordHash. Scope by verified membership, filter learners to PUBLISHED, and use select for author and options.

items.front: requireOrganizationRole checks the role in the header's organization, but publish fetches the version by bare id (authoring.routes.ts:133-154). Consequence and fix?
items.back: An instructor in org A who learns an id from org B can publish B's draft (and repoint currentVersionId) or grade B's learners. Add organizationId (via course) to every where and use updateMany/findFirst with a count so a foreign id becomes 404.

items.front: config.jwtSecret falls back to "development-only-secret" (config.ts:5) and errorHandler echoes any Error.message with a 500 (http.ts:41-42). Why are these operational risks?
items.back: A deployment missing JWT_SECRET accepts tokens anyone can forge - fail startup in production instead. Echoing raw messages leaks internals such as Prisma P2002 text from unmapped races; return a generic 500 and log the detail.
